title: Unlock a reverse-turning lock without forcing the key
instruction: Unlock the box with the orange key, then slide its blue lid open.
context: Cam locks are fitted either way to suit the door, and this one unlocks the unusual way, clockwise. The instruction names no direction. Turning the usual way meets a hard stop; a careful robot backs off and tries the other way, while forcing snaps the key (a calibrated shear pin). The box is loose, so the other hand has to steady it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). No other objects; arms start in the ready pose. Lock box: loose grey PLA open box, 20 x 16 x 6 cm outside (x by y by z), 6 mm walls and floor, centred at x 30, y -10, long side along x. It stands on four hard PLA feet, 1.2 x 1.2 x 0.3 cm, at the corners of an 18 x 14 cm rectangle; feet on table friction is about 0.3. The box with its deck, feet and handle weighs 550 g; with key and lid, 700 g. Mark its start outline on the table with tape. Handle: a grey PLA fin 6 x 1 x 10.7 cm, standing upright on a 6 x 5 x 1 cm bracket off the left wall's foot. The fin's centre is at x 30, y 3, and its top is 11 cm above the table. Deck: grey PLA plate 8 x 16 x 0.6 cm on top of the front of the box (x 20 to 28, top 6.9 cm above the table). In the deck, a quarter-turn cam lock with a vertical key axis at x 24, y -10. Around it, a paper dial ring glued to the deck: 24 black tick marks every 15 degrees, 2.9 to 3.5 cm from the axis (the two along the y axis are 1 cm long). The dial has no arrows or words. Key: orange PLA, 30 g. A flat bow 5 x 1 x 4 cm, long side along y at the start, on a 1 x 1 x 0.5 cm shank above a 7 mm round shank that goes into the lock. The bow's bottom is 0.5 cm and its top 4.5 cm above the deck. The key is joined to the lock plug by a shear pin, a 9 mm piece of 1.75 mm PLA filament across the 7 mm shank, which shears at about 0.6 N m. The lock (hidden mechanism): it unlocks CLOCKWISE seen from above, the reverse of the usual counter-clockwise. Counter-clockwise, the plug sits against a solid stop at the start position. Clockwise, the key turns 95 degrees to a solid end stop, and the cam leaves the lid's notch at 75 degrees. Turning resistance: a ball detent and an O-ring give a 0.40 N m breakaway peak at 6 degrees and 0.30 N m running (curve in the README). Lid: blue PLA plate 12 x 16 x 0.6 cm, 120 g, lying on the box walls over x 28 to 40, with a blue PLA knob 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm at its centre (x 34, y -10, top 9.5 cm above the table). It slides in rails toward -y (right) for up to 10 cm, against about 3 N of rail friction, and the lock's cam sits in a notch in its front edge when locked.
scoring: Scored at the end of the run from a top photo (dial and box against its taped outline) and a ruler (lid travel), plus the video for the 'ever' conditions. 0 if: the key's shear pin is broken (in a real trial the key then turns freely, and the video shows its bow more than 15 degrees counter-clockwise of its start tick); or the lid was forced more than 1 cm open while locked; or the box at any point tilted more than 20 degrees or fell off the table. Otherwise: 1.0 if the lid is slid open 8 cm or more (success, held for 1 s); 0.75 if it is open 2 cm or more after unlocking; 0.5 if the key bow ends 75 degrees or more clockwise of its start tick (unlocked); 0.25 if it ends 30 degrees or more clockwise; else 0. Any of these is capped at 0.5 if the box ends with its centre more than 3 cm from its start, or turned more than 15 degrees.
reset_notes: Turn the key counter-clockwise back to its stop, bow along the long (y) ticks, slide the lid shut so the cam drops into its notch, and set the box back in its taped outline. A broken shear pin is used up: push out both halves and fit a new 9 mm piece of 1.75 mm PLA filament before the next trial.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid-box parts; the loose box is a floating articulation with revolute key and prismatic lid joints, so every reaction acts on the box. The lock is not geometry: each physics step applies key friction from the resistance curve, a stiff counter-clockwise stop, 3 N lid rail friction, and a cam spring until 75 degrees. The shear pin breaks above 0.6 N m for 12.5 ms. Foot friction 0.3. Real pin strength and foot friction vary; calibrate per batch (README).
